source.title: Forgetting is Not Erasure: Recovering Latent Knowledge via Transport Keys

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. Some figures are described but their numerical values are not given in the text; those figure-only results are not extracted as numeric rows.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether a transport map can make representations from two checkpoints usable together through stitching, a conceptual test of V4. It uses sequential checkpoints of the same model rather than independently trained model pairs.
record.gate_note: The study concerns recovery after sequential training, not convergence with scale or cross-modal alignment. Rows are limited to reported stitched Task A accuracy, recovery rates, and directly relevant no-key or alignment-disruption controls. The anchor-efficiency plots are described qualitatively without numerical values; cited work is not treated as a result.
record.test_reason: The study uses model stitching with a fitted activation-space map as a diagnostic for continual-learning forgetting. The two networks stitched together are a checkpoint and its own fine-tuned successor, which share initialization and training history. They are not independently trained models, seeds, architectures or modalities. The question is whether Task A computation survives sequential training ('interface drift' vs erasure), not whether separately learned representations converge or are interchangeable. The reported numbers are the performance of the authors' transport-key method, against no-key and disrupted-key controls. So it bears on no version as stated. The closest version is V4, and the result is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Accurate. The authors conclude that much apparent forgetting is interface drift rather than erasure, recoverable by compact transport keys. They find recovery strongest at early stages, and note that the method needs the predecessor network, so it is a diagnostic.
record.recipe_differences: Uses paired-anchor activation-space transport keys and stitches post-update early computation to a predecessor's late computation; this is not a scale-convergence measurement or a comparison of independently trained models.
record.method_sensitivity: Recovery changes with interface stage. In the Mini ViT and domain-shift settings, no-key stitching is already strong at early interfaces; domain-shift results also differ between Keyed and Keyed+ conditions and their disruption controls.

fits_no_version.finding: After sequential training, early activations of the updated network can be realigned to the predecessor's late layers by a compact per-channel or cross-channel map. This recovers 85–92% of lost Task A accuracy at s1 on CIFAR-100, falling to about 50% at s3 and failing at the last stage. Paired-anchor correspondence matters: the shuffled-correspondence control drops to 0.184 at s2 under domain shift.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A network's representations before and after fine-tuning on a new task stay linearly or channel-wise stitchable at early layers, with stitchability declining with depth.

record.problems: Experiments cover only vision classification and at most three tasks; model sizes and seeds are not stated. Numerical uncertainty is not reported. Several stage-wise outcomes are given only as recovery percentages or qualitative descriptions, and Table 2's domain-shift keyed value (0.752) differs from Table 4's Keyed value (0.705) without an explanation in the text.
record.rows_left_out: No figure-only numeric values were extracted for the anchor-efficiency and domain-shift control graphs (Figures 4–6); the text describes those outcomes qualitatively. Other results about task accuracy not tied to stitched mapping were left out.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no cross-model alignment measure.
No vision-language or paired image-caption data.
No models trained from different random initializations.
No mapping between independently trained models (seeds, architectures, data). The study only realigns a fine-tuned checkpoint to its own predecessor. No relative representations or unpaired mapping.
No interpretable features or circuits compared across models.
No similarity metrics compared; domain shift concerns training tasks, not evaluation inputs of a convergence measure.
No measure of convergence level or its causes.

missing.what: No-key stitching at s1 under CIFAR-10→SVHN already reaches 0.619 (vs post-update 0.154), so the key's added value is smaller than the post-update baseline implies.

record.verdict_notes: The record treated predecessor/successor checkpoints as V4 model pairs. These networks share initialization and most training, so stitchability between them says little about convergence or interchangeability of independently learned representations. I reclassified the study as T4 (it uses stitching as a tool) and removed the V4 labels. r9 and r12 are the same value (Table 2 reports Keyed+). In the Mini ViT, keyed and no-key stitching are equal at b0, so that recovery is not due to the mapping. Single-author preprint; no uncertainty, seeds or model sizes reported.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size or capability sweep and no comparison of representation alignment across independently trained architectures, objectives, or datasets.
No paired image-caption evaluation or vision-language model comparison.
No comparison across random initialization seeds or analysis of shared features or subspaces.

Tests stitching across sequential checkpoints of the same model in vision classification. Does not test independently trained model pairs, relative representations, unpaired mapping, or layer stitching across independently trained networks.
No recurring interpretable features, neurons, SAE features, or circuits are measured.
Does not compare similarity metrics, their settings, or in- versus out-of-distribution inputs as tests of convergence.
Does not test whether convergence plateaus or whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Early-stage stitching in the reported vision continual-learning settings
reader_labels.reason: Stitched evaluation recovers most lost Task A accuracy at early interfaces in the Split CIFAR-100, three-task, domain-shift, and Mini ViT results (r1, r5, r9, r12, r18).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Later stages and domain-shift stage s2
reader_labels.reason: Recovery is incomplete and declines with stage; it fails at the latest reported stages, and domain-shift stage-s2 results remain below pre-update accuracy (r2, r3, r6, r7, r8, r14, r16, r19, r20, r21).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: Keyed stitching gives 0.386 versus a post-update accuracy of 0.392 and is reported as −1.7% recovery, so mapping fails at this interface (r4).
